1.explanation: This example uses the same pattern as the “Expansion” story in Carbon’s DataTable. You can run it, open the browser DevTools, and inspect the generated <table>. You will see that the expansion <td> in each row has a `headers="expand"` attribute, but there is no corresponding `<th id="expand">` in the table head. Running the IBM Equal Access Accessibility Checker on this page will reproduce the violation “The ‘headers’ attribute value ‘expand’ does not reference a valid ‘id’ in this document.” This minimal snippet isolates the missing id issue and makes it easier to debug and verify a fix.
1.bug_scenario: When you render a Carbon DataTable with row-level expansion (using TableExpandHeader and TableExpandRow), the expansion cell in each row is given a “headers” attribute pointing at an id (“expand”) that never actually exists on the corresponding . In the DOM you’ll see: • In the header: …… (no id) …… • In each body row: Because there is no in the table, IBM Equal Access Accessibility Checker flags “The ‘headers’ attribute value ‘expand’ does not reference a valid ‘id’ in this document.”
